title: Tafsir annotation — approved record (v1.0.0)
description: One verified tafsir annotation unit: a pinned source text, the machine's proposal, and the human-approved labels. Tafsir-agnostic and UI-agnostic — no tafsir work is privileged over another, and no consumer needs any AI to read it. The source text is never the stored truth: start_char/end_char index into a pinned file (source_id + sha256) and text is a convenience copy that must equal the sliced source exactly. A published dataset is a JSON array whose items each validate against this schema.
$comment: Cross-field rules that JSON Schema draft 2020-12 cannot express (no arithmetic, no $data extension): source.end_char MUST be greater than source.start_char; quran.ayah_end MUST be >= quran.ayah; and text MUST equal source_file[source.start_char:source.end_char] over the pinned file decoded as UTF-8 bytes-as-is. Validators and exporters MUST enforce these three in code — schema/example_approved.json is checked against both the schema and the offsets.

annotation_id.description: Stable public id, unique inside a dataset: "<tafsir.id>-<window key>-<move id>". ASCII, no whitespace.

quran.description: The verse, or verse range, this unit comments on.

ayah_end.description: Optional. Last ayah of a multi-ayah range; must be >= ayah (cross-field rule — check in code).

tafsir.description: Which tafsir work the text belongs to. Data, never code: adding a work means adding values, not editing this schema.

id.description: Lowercase slug, no spaces: the work's short Latin name (al_tabari, al_baghawi, al_sadi).

name.description: Human-readable work name in its own language.

source.description: Pointer into the pinned plain-text source file. These offsets are the ground truth.

source_id.description: Stable id of the pinned file; convention "<tafsir.id>_<surah>_<ayah>".

sha256.description: SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the pinned source file bytes, or null when the pin is unavailable. Consumers re-hash the file and refuse to publish records whose pin does not match.

start_char.description: Inclusive start: 0-based index of the first character, counted in Unicode code points over the source file decoded as UTF-8 bytes-as-is (no newline translation).

end_char.description: Exclusive end (Python slice semantics); must be greater than start_char (cross-field rule — check in code).

labels.description: Two independent label sets: how the author argued (source_method) and what the passage contains (content_type). Several values per set are normal. Together they must not both be empty — a pure takhrij or content passage may have no method, so the rule is expressed as anyOf rather than as minItems on each list.

text.description: Convenience copy of the pinned source slice. MUST equal source_file[start_char:end_char] exactly, including spaces, newlines and \r characters. Never store a trimmed, normalized or edited variant here; re-verify before publishing.

verification.description: Result of comparing text against the pinned source slice when the record was exported.

text_fidelity.description: exact = text is the source slice character for character; partial = text lies inside the slice but the boundaries need review; modified = text differs from the slice (an editorial change reached the text field); not_found = the source file or the slice could not be resolved.

strict_match.description: True only when text == source[start_char:end_char] character for character.

normalized_match.description: True when the comparison also holds after whitespace collapsing and tashkeel removal. It can be true while strict_match is false: that is a warning, not a pass.

ai_proposal.description: Immutable snapshot of what the machine proposed before human review. Kept for traceability and audit; never publishable content on its own.

end_char.description: Exclusive end; must be greater than start_char.

labels.description: The machine's label sets. Unlike the approved labels, both lists may be empty here: the classifier is allowed to abstain (certainty: insufficient).

certainty.description: How explicit the textual marker behind the proposal is.

score.description: Auditable rule score (marker + function evidence + attribution + boundary).

route.description: Triage decision: auto_candidate may be batched ahead; specialist must be decided by a human specialist.

review.description: Human review state plus audit trail.

status.description: Only "approved" is publishable content. ai_proposed and under_review are working states; rejected is kept for audit.

reviewer_role.description: Role of the human who made the decision.

reviewed_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the current status.

changes.description: Ordered audit log of reviewer actions; empty when approved without edits. Each entry needs 'at' and 'action'; the before/after state and context keys are kept as recorded by the review tool.

dateTime.description: RFC 3339 date-time, e.g. 2026-09-28T12:00:00Z. The pattern makes the check portable: in draft 2020-12 the format keyword is only an annotation unless the validator enables format assertion.

sourceMethodList.description: The evidence the author used. Several values allowed; empty allowed (a pure takhrij or content passage may have no method).

contentTypeList.description: What the passage contains. Several values allowed; empty allowed.

sourceMethod.description: M_QURAN قرآن بالقرآن · M_SUNNAH سنة · M_SAHABA صحابة · M_TABIIN تابعون · M_LUGHA لغة وغريب · M_QIRAAT قراءات · M_NUZUL أسباب نزول · M_SIRA مغازي وسير · M_ISRAILIYYAT إسرائيليات · M_RAY رأي واجتهاد

contentType.description: C_FIQH فقه وأحكام · C_BALAGHA بلاغة · C_SHIR شعر · C_FADAIL فضائل · C_TAKHRIJ تخريج وحكم حديثي · C_NUZUL أسباب نزول · C_ISRAILIYYAT إسرائيليات · C_TAFSIR بيان معنى
